transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is… I can’t keep my head clear lately, especially at work. I’m a therapist, so I’m supposed to be really present with clients, obviously, and lately I’ll be sitting there and suddenly realize I’ve lost track of what they were saying. Not because I don’t care—if anything I’m trying really hard to focus—but it’s like my brain just slips off the conversation.

And then with notes, I’ll reread the same chart note over and over, like three or four times, and it still won’t stick. I’ll get to the end and realize I don’t really know what I just read. Even simple decisions I used to make without thinking—how to word something, what to prioritize, what the next step should be—I just freeze. It’s embarrassing, honestly, and it’s starting to scare me because this used to be stuff I could handle.
Have you been feeling depressed lately?

I… I don’t know. I mean, that’s kind of hard for me to answer cleanly. I wouldn’t say I’m walking around labeling it that way in my head, exactly. I know something feels off, and I know I don’t feel like myself, but when you ask “depressed,” I start second-guessing what counts.

Like, I can tell you I’ve been struggling, and I feel pretty weighed down by it, but I’m not sure if that’s the same thing as being depressed or if I’m just stressed and overwhelmed and not handling it as well as I should. I guess… maybe? But I don’t know how to measure that.
Have you been feeling down most days?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t know if I’d say “most days” in a clear way, because I don’t really track it like that, and I think I tend to talk myself out of naming it.

There are definitely days where I feel… heavy, I guess, or kind of low, but then I’ll tell myself maybe I’m just tired or stressed or having an off day. So I can’t confidently say, “yes, most days,” but I also can’t say it’s nothing. It’s been present enough that I’ve noticed I don’t feel like my usual self.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually enjoy less than before?

Yeah… actually, yes. That’s probably one of the clearer things, now that you ask it that way.

Like, my guitar has literally been sitting in the corner of my room, and I keep looking at it like I should pick it up, because normally that’s one of the things that resets me. I used to just mess around with it without even thinking, even if I only had ten minutes. But lately it’s like… I see it, I know I used to want to play, and then I just don’t. It feels like too much effort for something that won’t really do anything, which is weird because I know it used to feel good.

And I’ve been bailing on soccer more than I want to admit. Same with volunteering at the shelter. I’ll tell myself I’m just busy or I’ll go next time, but if I’m being honest, part of it is that I just can’t seem to make myself care enough in the moment to go. And then I feel bad about it, because these are things I chose, you know? They weren’t obligations someone forced on me.

Even when I try to do the “good” things, like cooking something decent or going for a hike, it doesn’t really land. I’ll go through the steps, but it feels kind of empty, like I’m just acting out what I’m supposed to enjoy. There’s this sense of, I don’t know, “what’s the point?” Not in a dramatic way, just… flat. Like the color’s been turned down on all of it.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest in things like guitar, soccer, and volunteering?

I think it’s been about a month. Maybe a little hard to pin down exactly, but that’s when I really started noticing it — around the time the clinic lost some staff and my schedule got shifted.

I started doing more late-evening coverage, and there’s been a lot more crisis paperwork on top of everything, and I think that’s when the things I normally care about started feeling like… extra weight instead of relief. At first I told myself it was just because my hours were weird and I was tired after work, so of course I wasn’t picking up the guitar or making it to soccer or volunteering. But then it kept happening, week after week, and even on days when I technically had time, I still didn’t really want to do any of it.

So… yeah, about a month, since all that changed at work.
Do you feel these changes started because of the shift in your workload at the clinic?

I think so, yeah… at least that’s when it really started becoming noticeable. I don’t know if I can say it’s the only reason, because that feels too neat, but the timing lines up pretty clearly.

When the clinic lost staff and my schedule shifted into more late-evening coverage, and then the crisis paperwork got heavier, that’s when I started realizing I wasn’t doing the things I usually do. Like, it’s been about a month of that. At first I kept explaining it away as, “Well, of course I’m not going to soccer, I’m working later,” or “Of course I’m not playing guitar, I’m wiped out,” but then it wasn’t just the schedule. Even when I had the chance, I still didn’t really want to.

So… yeah. About a month, and it seems tied to that change at the clinic, or at least it started around then.
Have you been worrying a lot lately?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I worry about things, but I don’t know if I’d call it “a lot” in some separate, obvious way.

Like, I do think about work and whether I’m keeping up, and I can get stuck turning things over in my head, but I also don’t know where the line is between normal worrying and something more than that. Sometimes it just feels like background noise rather than me sitting there actively panicking or anything.

So… maybe some, yeah, but I haven’t really been tracking it the way I have with the not-enjoying-things part. I’m not sure it’s the main thing I’ve noticed.
Over the past month, have you been feeling sad or down?

I’m… not completely sure how to answer that, honestly. I wouldn’t say I’ve been walking around crying or anything like that, or like there’s one clear mood I can point to all day every day and say, “Yes, that’s sadness.”

But I have felt kind of… low, I guess. More flat than anything. Like things feel heavier than they should, and it’s harder to get myself emotionally “up” for stuff. I don’t know if that counts as sad or down in the way you mean. Some days I think I’m just tired or worn out, and then other days I catch myself realizing I haven’t really felt okay for a while.

So… yeah, maybe down, but it’s not always dramatic. It’s more like this dull, dragged-out feeling that’s been there a lot lately.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period like this where you lost interest in things and felt low for at least a couple of weeks?

I’m trying to think… I don’t know if I can say there was another clear period like this before. Not in a way where I can confidently say, “Yes, that was the same thing for two weeks or more.”

I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before, like anyone, where I was stressed or kind of withdrawn for a bit, but I don’t remember it feeling like this exact combination of not really wanting to do things and feeling low in this dull, persistent way. Or maybe I just wasn’t paying as much attention then, I’m not sure.

So… I guess my answer is I don’t really know of another episode like this. Nothing that stands out clearly.
Have you had trouble sleeping lately?

Yeah… sleep has been pretty bad lately. It’s not even that I don’t feel tired — I’ll get home and I’m exhausted, like I should be able to just collapse and sleep, but then once I’m actually in bed my brain won’t really shut off.

I end up lying there for hours, kind of replaying the whole day. Not always even in a productive way, just going back over conversations or things I did or didn’t do, and it feels like I’m stuck there even though my body is tired. And then if I do finally fall asleep, it doesn’t feel solid. I’ll wake up before my alarm, sometimes way before, and it’s that awful feeling where you’re awake but not rested at all. Like technically I slept, but it feels like I barely did.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite lately?

Yeah… actually, yes. I didn’t really connect it at first, because it wasn’t like I woke up one day and thought, “I’m not eating anymore.” It’s more like most days I just don’t feel hungry until something reminds me that I haven’t eaten.

Like someone will mention lunch, or I’ll see the time and realize it’s already late, and then I’ll think, “Oh, I guess I skipped breakfast,” or sometimes breakfast and lunch. It’s not exactly on purpose. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything. Food just doesn’t really occur to me the same way, and when it does, it feels like more effort than it should.

I’ve noticed my pants are looser too, which is probably the part that made me realize it’s not just in my head. I keep having to pull them up more than usual. So… yeah, my appetite has definitely been off.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Yeah… I mean, I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I want to be clear about that. It’s not like I’ve sat down and thought through some way to do it.

But I have been having these thoughts that scare me, honestly. Like… sometimes I’ll think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. Not necessarily that I want to do something, but more like if I could just not have to keep doing this, or not have to feel this way, that would be easier. And then I get scared because I know that’s not a small thing to be thinking.

It feels awful even saying it out loud, because part of me wants to explain it away or make it sound less serious. But yeah… those thoughts have been there.
Over the past month, have you felt down or depressed for most of the day nearly every day?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. Like, “most of the day nearly every day” sounds so specific, and I haven’t exactly been tracking it hour by hour or anything.

I guess I would say I’ve felt pretty low a lot of the time, but I’m not sure if it’s literally most of the day every single day. Some days it kind of comes in waves, or I can get distracted for a while and not notice it as much, and then it’s back. Other days it feels like it’s just sitting there the whole time, like background noise I can’t turn off.

So… I don’t want to exaggerate and say yes if that means something very exact, but I also don’t want to pretend I’ve been fine. I haven’t. It’s been there a lot this past month.
When you start worrying, is it hard to stop or control the worrying?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I don’t know if what I do is “worrying” in the way you mean it.

Like, I definitely get stuck thinking about things sometimes, and I can go over the same thing in my head more than I probably need to. But I’m not sure if I’d describe it as this constant worry that I can’t control. It’s more like… once a thought is there, I may sit with it for a while, or keep circling back to it, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as not being able to stop.

I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether I can control it or not. Sometimes I can distract myself, and other times it just kind of keeps running in the background. So… maybe sometimes, but I don’t feel confident saying it’s definitely hard to stop in a clear way.
In the past month, have you found yourself feeling hopeless?

I’m not sure. I mean… I know what the word means generally, but I don’t know if I’d label what I’ve been feeling as “hopeless” exactly.

There have definitely been moments where I feel really discouraged, like I can’t see how things are supposed to get better, or I just feel kind of stuck in the same place emotionally. But then I hesitate, because “hopeless” sounds so final, like I’ve completely given up, and I don’t know if that’s true.

I guess I’d say there are times where it feels hard to imagine things improving, but I’m not sure how constant that is or whether it fully counts as hopelessness. It’s more like… I don’t have a clear sense of what would make things feel okay again.
Did these symptoms begin after the staffing changes and schedule shift at the clinic?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, that’s when I started noticing it, or at least that’s when it seemed to become a real pattern.

It’s been about a month now, since the clinic lost staff and everything kind of shifted around. My schedule changed into more late-evening coverage, and there’s been heavier crisis paperwork too. I don’t know if I can say it was like a single day where I woke up and everything felt different, but that whole change is basically when this started building up and not really letting up.
Over the past month, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know if I would’ve immediately used the word “worthless,” but that is kind of what it turns into in my head.

Like, if I miss one detail in a note, or if I realize I forgot to return a call right away, I don’t just think, “Okay, I need to fix that.” It becomes this whole thing where I’m telling myself I’m useless, or that I shouldn’t be doing this work if I can’t keep up with basic things. And then I start thinking I’m letting the clients down, and everyone at the clinic down, because other people are already stretched and I’m just adding to the problem.

It feels excessive when I say it out loud, because realistically I know people forget things or make mistakes sometimes, but in the moment it feels like proof that I’m failing at everything. So… yeah, there’s been a lot of guilt, and it gets pretty harsh.
Even when work isn’t in front of you, do you still feel this low?

I’m not totally sure how to separate it, honestly. Like, work is usually the thing my mind grabs onto first, because it’s the easiest explanation — there’s always some note, some message, some thing I didn’t do perfectly that my brain can point to.

But even when I’m not physically at work or actively doing anything for it, I don’t exactly feel… fine. It’s more like the low feeling follows me home, if that makes sense. I might not be thinking about a specific task every second, but I still feel kind of weighed down or flat. And then sometimes I start wondering if it’s really about work, or if work just gives shape to something that’s already there.

So, I guess yes, but I’m hesitant saying that because I don’t want to make it sound like it’s completely constant every minute. There are moments where I’m distracted or I’m not actively focused on it. But overall, even when work isn’t right in front of me, I don’t feel like I fully come back to normal.

doctor.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
doctor.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: I'm here because lately I can't keep my head clear at work—I lose track of what clients are saying, reread the same chart note over and over, and then freeze on simple decisions I used to handle.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code, S031.

patient.answer:
I guess the main thing is… I can’t keep my head clear lately, especially at work. I’m a therapist, so I’m supposed to be really present with clients, obviously, and lately I’ll be sitting there and suddenly realize I’ve lost track of what they were saying. Not because I don’t care—if anything I’m trying really hard to focus—but it’s like my brain just slips off the conversation.

And then with notes, I’ll reread the same chart note over and over, like three or four times, and it still won’t stick. I’ll get to the end and realize I don’t really know what I just read. Even simple decisions I used to make without thinking—how to word something, what to prioritize, what the next step should be—I just freeze. It’s embarrassing, honestly, and it’s starting to scare me because this used to be stuff I could handle.

When the clinic lost staff and my schedule shifted into more late-evening coverage, and then the crisis paperwork got heavier, that’s when I started realizing I wasn’t doing the things I usually do. Like, I do think about work and whether I’m keeping up, and I can get stuck turning things over in my head, but I also don’t know where the line is between normal worrying and something more than that. Sometimes it just feels like background noise rather than me sitting there actively panicking or anything.

So… maybe some, yeah, but I haven’t really been tracking it the way I have with the not-enjoying-things part. I’m not sure it’s the main thing I’ve noticed.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has had depressed mood, a core symptom needed to distinguish a depressive episode from stress-related or anxiety-related conditions.
doctor.question: Over the past month, have you been feeling sad or down?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depressed mood (feeling sad or down), but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific depressed mood item.

patient.answer:
I’m… not completely sure how to answer that, honestly. I wouldn’t say I’ve been walking around crying or anything like that, or like there’s one clear mood I can point to all day every day and say, “Yes, that’s sadness.”

But I have felt kind of… low, I guess. More flat than anything. Like things feel heavier than they should, and it’s harder to get myself emotionally “up” for stuff. I don’t know if that counts as sad or down in the way you mean. Some days I think I’m just tired or worn out, and then other days I catch myself realizing I haven’t really felt okay for a while.

So… yeah, maybe down, but it’s not always dramatic. It’s more like this dull, dragged-out feeling that’s been there a lot lately.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a history of prior depressive episodes to distinguish a single current depressive episode from recurrent depression.
doctor.question: Before this past month, have you ever had another period like this where you lost interest in things and felt low for at least a couple of weeks?

target_item.reason: The question asks about any previous episodes before the current past month, but the symptom profile only describes the current episode duration and does not provide information about past similar periods.

patient.answer:
I’m trying to think… I don’t know if I can say there was another clear period like this before. Not in a way where I can confidently say, “Yes, that was the same thing for two weeks or more.”

I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before, like anyone, where I was stressed or kind of withdrawn for a bit, but I don’t remember it feeling like this exact combination of not really wanting to do things and feeling low in this dull, persistent way. Or maybe I just wasn’t paying as much attention then, I’m not sure.

So… I guess my answer is I don’t really know of another episode like this. Nothing that stands out clearly.

inference.note: No prior clear depressive episode established; current month-long anhedonia/low mood remains consistent with single depressive episode or stress-related disorder. GAD and mild neurocognitive/organic causes not yet excluded.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a core depressive neurovegetative symptom to distinguish a major depressive episode from stress-related adjustment symptoms or generalized anxiety.
doctor.question: Have you had trouble sleeping lately?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: I get home tired but then lie there for hours replaying the day, and if I do fall asleep I wake up before my alarm feeling like I barely slept.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks about trouble sleeping lately, which matches sleep disturbance.

patient.answer:
Yeah… sleep has been pretty bad lately. It’s not even that I don’t feel tired — I’ll get home and I’m exhausted, like I should be able to just collapse and sleep, but then once I’m actually in bed my brain won’t really shut off.

I end up lying there for hours, kind of replaying the whole day. Not always even in a productive way, just going back over conversations or things I did or didn’t do, and it feels like I’m stuck there even though my body is tired. And then if I do finally fall asleep, it doesn’t feel solid. I’ll wake up before my alarm, sometimes way before, and it’s that awful feeling where you’re awake but not rested at all. Like technically I slept, but it feels like I barely did.

inference.note: Insomnia adds support for a depressive episode; current symptoms include anhedonia, low/flat mood, impaired concentration, and sleep disturbance for about 1 month. This makes F32.9 more likely. F06.7 is less favored because symptoms are temporally linked to work stress and accompanied by mood/anxiety features rather than a primary cognitive disorder.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the symptoms represent a major depressive episode by checking for a core vegetative symptom that would help distinguish depression from stress-related adjustment or generalized anxiety.
doctor.question: Have you noticed a change in your appetite lately?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Most days I don't feel hungry until someone reminds me to eat, and my pants have gotten loose because I've been skipping meals without really meaning to.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about changes in appetite lately.

patient.answer:
Yeah… actually, yes. I didn’t really connect it at first, because it wasn’t like I woke up one day and thought, “I’m not eating anymore.” It’s more like most days I just don’t feel hungry until something reminds me that I haven’t eaten.

Like someone will mention lunch, or I’ll see the time and realize it’s already late, and then I’ll think, “Oh, I guess I skipped breakfast,” or sometimes breakfast and lunch. It’s not exactly on purpose. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything. Food just doesn’t really occur to me the same way, and when it does, it feels like more effort than it should.

I’ve noticed my pants are looser too, which is probably the part that made me realize it’s not just in my head. I keep having to pull them up more than usual. So… yeah, my appetite has definitely been off.

inference.note: Appetite/weight loss and insomnia over ~1 month strengthen a depressive episode. Recurrent depression is less supported because the patient does not endorse a clear prior episode, so F33.9 is removed. Adjustment disorder remains possible given clear onset after work stressor; GAD remains possible but is less central.

doctor.intent: Assess suicidal ideation to determine whether this is a major depressive episode rather than stress-related or generalized anxiety symptoms, and to evaluate immediate safety risk.
doctor.question: Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I don't have a plan to hurt myself, but I keep having these thoughts like it would be easier if I didn't wake up, and that scares me because I know what that can mean.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I want to be clear about that. It’s not like I’ve sat down and thought through some way to do it.

But I have been having these thoughts that scare me, honestly. Like… sometimes I’ll think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. Not necessarily that I want to do something, but more like if I could just not have to keep doing this, or not have to feel this way, that would be easier. And then I get scared because I know that’s not a small thing to be thinking.

It feels awful even saying it out loud, because part of me wants to explain it away or make it sound less serious. But yeah… those thoughts have been there.

inference.note: Added appetite/weight loss, insomnia, impaired concentration, anhedonia, low mood, and passive death wishes over ~1 month, making a depressive episode more likely and more severe than unspecified depression; adjusted F32.9 to F32.1. Stressor-linked symptoms keep adjustment disorder in the differential. GAD remains possible but less favored.

doctor.intent: Distinguish major depressive episode from adjustment disorder and generalized anxiety by assessing whether the depressed/low mood is present most of the day nearly every day, which is a key criterion for MDE and less consistent with GAD alone.
doctor.question: Over the past month, have you felt down or depressed for most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about depressed mood most of the day nearly every day, but the provided symptom profile does not include a depressed mood item.

patient.answer:
I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. Like, “most of the day nearly every day” sounds so specific, and I haven’t exactly been tracking it hour by hour or anything.

I guess I would say I’ve felt pretty low a lot of the time, but I’m not sure if it’s literally most of the day every single day. Some days it kind of comes in waves, or I can get distracted for a while and not notice it as much, and then it’s back. Other days it feels like it’s just sitting there the whole time, like background noise I can’t turn off.

So… I don’t want to exaggerate and say yes if that means something very exact, but I also don’t want to pretend I’ve been fine. I haven’t. It’s been there a lot this past month.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's excessive worry is difficult to control, which best distinguishes generalized anxiety disorder from a depressive episode or adjustment disorder at this point.
doctor.question: When you start worrying, is it hard to stop or control the worrying?

target_item.reason: The question is about difficulty controlling worry/anxiety, which is not covered by the listed depressive symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I don’t know if what I do is “worrying” in the way you mean it.

Like, I definitely get stuck thinking about things sometimes, and I can go over the same thing in my head more than I probably need to. But I’m not sure if I’d describe it as this constant worry that I can’t control. It’s more like… once a thought is there, I may sit with it for a while, or keep circling back to it, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as not being able to stop.

I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether I can control it or not. Sometimes I can distract myself, and other times it just kind of keeps running in the background. So… maybe sometimes, but I don’t feel confident saying it’s definitely hard to stop in a clear way.

doctor.intent: Differentiate major depressive episode from adjustment disorder by establishing whether there is a core depressed mood symptom despite the patient's uncertainty.
doctor.question: In the past month, have you found yourself feeling hopeless?

target_item.reason: The question asks specifically about feeling hopeless, but the provided symptom profile does not include hopelessness as a distinct item. The closest items involve worthlessness/guilt or suicidal thoughts, but those are not the same as hopelessness.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I mean… I know what the word means generally, but I don’t know if I’d label what I’ve been feeling as “hopeless” exactly.

There have definitely been moments where I feel really discouraged, like I can’t see how things are supposed to get better, or I just feel kind of stuck in the same place emotionally. But then I hesitate, because “hopeless” sounds so final, like I’ve completely given up, and I don’t know if that’s true.

I guess I’d say there are times where it feels hard to imagine things improving, but I’m not sure how constant that is or whether it fully counts as hopelessness. It’s more like… I don’t have a clear sense of what would make things feel okay again.

Yeah… I think so. I mean, that’s when I started noticing it, or at least that’s when it seemed to become a real pattern.

It’s been about a month now, since the clinic lost staff and everything kind of shifted around. My schedule changed into more late-evening coverage, and there’s been heavier crisis paperwork too. I don’t know if I can say it was like a single day where I woke up and everything felt different, but that whole change is basically when this started building up and not really letting up.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a major depressive episode from an adjustment disorder by determining whether the patient has clinically significant guilt or worthlessness, a core depressive symptom not explained by stress alone.
doctor.question: Over the past month, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: If I miss one detail in a note or forget to return a call right away, I keep telling myself I'm useless and that I'm letting the clients and everyone at the clinic down.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks about feeling worthless or excessively guilty over the past month.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I don’t know if I would’ve immediately used the word “worthless,” but that is kind of what it turns into in my head.

Like, if I miss one detail in a note, or if I realize I forgot to return a call right away, I don’t just think, “Okay, I need to fix that.” It becomes this whole thing where I’m telling myself I’m useless, or that I shouldn’t be doing this work if I can’t keep up with basic things. And then I start thinking I’m letting the clients down, and everyone at the clinic down, because other people are already stretched and I’m just adding to the problem.

It feels excessive when I say it out loud, because realistically I know people forget things or make mistakes sometimes, but in the moment it feels like proof that I’m failing at everything. So… yeah, there’s been a lot of guilt, and it gets pretty harsh.

inference.note: Added depressive cognitions (worthlessness/excessive guilt) on top of anhedonia, insomnia, appetite/weight loss, impaired concentration, low mood, and passive death wishes over ~1 month, which strengthens a major depressive episode and makes F41.1 less likely.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the depressive symptoms are pervasive rather than mainly tied to the identifiable work stressor, to distinguish major depressive episode from adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.
doctor.question: Even when work isn’t in front of you, do you still feel this low?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether a generally low mood persists outside of work, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific depressed mood symptom item.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to separate it, honestly. Like, work is usually the thing my mind grabs onto first, because it’s the easiest explanation — there’s always some note, some message, some thing I didn’t do perfectly that my brain can point to.

But even when I’m not physically at work or actively doing anything for it, I don’t exactly feel… fine. It’s more like the low feeling follows me home, if that makes sense. I might not be thinking about a specific task every second, but I still feel kind of weighed down or flat. And then sometimes I start wondering if it’s really about work, or if work just gives shape to something that’s already there.

So, I guess yes, but I’m hesitant saying that because I don’t want to make it sound like it’s completely constant every minute. There are moments where I’m distracted or I’m not actively focused on it. But overall, even when work isn’t right in front of me, I don’t feel like I fully come back to normal.

inference.note: Symptoms over ~1 month now meet a full major depressive episode: anhedonia, low mood/flatness, insomnia, decreased appetite/weight loss, impaired concentration, excessive guilt/worthlessness, and passive death wishes. Although onset followed a work stressor, the syndrome extends beyond a typical adjustment reaction, so F43.23 is ruled out.
